item.title: Teach a Picture Card Game
item.prompt_text: Teach a friend a game with picture cards. Put five cards face up between two players. On each turn, choose two and say what they have in common. If the other person agrees, keep the pair and put out two new cards. If they disagree, leave both cards. After six turns each, count the pairs. Explain the rules with one example.
item.target_grammar: Imperatives for setup; if clauses for agreement; first and after for order.
item.fluency_objective: Separate setup, taking a turn and finishing. Give your example while explaining a turn.
item.pronunciation_objective: Stress pair and agree. Pause after if they disagree so the listener can hear the contrast.

cues.text: Say where and how many cards to put out.
Explain a turn and give an example of a pair.
Explain what changes if the other person agrees or disagrees.
Explain when the game ends and how to win.

item.model_opening: First, put five picture cards face up between us.
item.model_answer: First, put five picture cards face up between us. On your turn, choose two cards and say what they have in common. For example, an apple and a pear are both fruit. If I agree, keep the pair and put out two new cards. If I disagree, leave both cards where they are. After six turns each, count the pairs. The player with the most pairs wins.
